question: Should OpenClaw guarantee a config-owned pre-deadline warning for native and ACP sub-agent runs, and should that warning share lifecycle infrastructure with inactivity recovery?
rationale: The feature adds public configuration and defines cross-runtime timing and delivery guarantees; source inspection can establish that it is missing, but cannot choose the permanent API boundary or guarantee level.

options.title: Shared lifecycle monitor
options.body: Add one config-owned intervention scheduler and child-control seam that supports absolute-deadline warnings now and inactivity nudges through separate policy later.

options.title: Deadline warning only
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped config-level pre-timeout warning for native and ACP runs without committing to the broader inactivity-monitor design.

options.title: Decline warning surface
options.body: Keep the hard timeout contract unchanged and rely on unlimited or longer timeouts plus task-level checkpoint instructions.

recommendation.title: Shared lifecycle monitor
recommendation.body: Add one config-owned intervention scheduler and child-control seam that supports absolute-deadline warnings now and inactivity nudges through separate policy later.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged the timeout configuration and has the broadest recent history across the affected native, ACP, configuration, and completion lifecycle surfaces.
